description: Somos a Artemis Innovators, uma equipe de estudantes do 9º ano apaixonados por ciência, tecnologia e inovação. No desafio Abandonados, mas não Esquecidos, queremos explorar e apresentar as histórias dos equipamentos deixados na Lua e em Marte. Buscamos pessoas interessadas em exploração espacial, desenvolvimento, design, dados e multimídia para contribuir com diferentes ideias e habilidades.
summary:
Spacy Legacy is an interactive educational platform developed for the *Abandoned but Not Forgotten* challenge, with the goal of preserving and sharing the scientific legacy of space exploration.

The project features 27 space artifacts associated with missions to the Moon, Mars, asteroids, and deep space. Through a digital museum, visitors can explore historical information, images, locations, scientific discoveries, and a timeline of NASA missions.

Its main highlight is an interactive simulator that allows users to select real space missions, configure spacecraft components, and observe how environmental factors affect their operation through simplified educational models.

The platform also explores theoretical possibilities for reusing space equipment, connecting sustainability, engineering, resource savings, and fundamental robotics concepts.

With accessibility features and multilingual support, Spacy Legacy aims to transform scientific knowledge into engaging educational experiences, bringing children, students, and space enthusiasts closer to the wonders of space exploration.

Our purpose is to show that a mission may end, but its legacy lives on

details:
Spacy Legacy — Interactive Space Heritage Museum

Overview and Functionality

Spacy Legacy is an interactive educational platform developed for the Abandoned but Not Forgotten challenge of the NASA Space Apps Challenge. Our goal is to preserve, share, and give new meaning to the history of space equipment left behind on the Moon, Mars, asteroids, and in deep space, connecting students and space enthusiasts with the scientific discoveries made possible by these missions.

The platform operates as a digital museum, featuring 27 space artifacts researched using official NASA documents and the NASA Space Science Data Coordinated Archive (NSSDCA).

Visitors can explore historical records, images, 3D representations, locations, scientific objectives, operational status, and mission timelines. Each artifact also presents conceptual possibilities for reusing its components in future space exploration activities.

Space Mission Simulator

One of Spacy Legacy's main features is its educational space engineering simulator.

Users can select a real space mission and configure components such as power sources, batteries, thermal protection systems, wheels, computers, and communication equipment.

The system simulates the spacecraft's operation over time, considering factors such as:

  • Energy generation and consumption.
  • Day-night cycles and extreme temperatures.
  • Dust accumulation and Martian dust storms.
  • Radiation exposure and component wear.
  • Communication capabilities with Earth.
  • Hibernation and potential operational failures.

At the end of the simulation, users receive a performance evaluation of their configuration, allowing them to compare the simulated mission duration with the actual historical mission.

The simulator uses simplified models for educational purposes. Its goal is to teach engineering decisions and limitations, helping students understand why certain technologies survive longer than others in extraterrestrial environments.

Technologies and System Architecture

The system was developed using modern web development and software engineering technologies:

  • React and Vite: Used to build the interactive user interface, digital museum, and educational pages.
  • ASP.NET Core (.NET 10): Used for backend development, scientific data management, simulation processing, and narration content generation.
  • Brazilian Sign Language API: Integrated with VLibras, an initiative of the Brazilian Federal Government, to improve accessibility through Brazilian Sign Language (Libras).
  • Speech API: Converts text into audio, enabling narrated content for users.
  • Docker Compose and nginx: Used to organize, integrate, and run the system's services in a standardized environment.

The architecture separates the visual interface, scientific processing, and accessibility services, making the platform easier to maintain, expand, and improve.

Use of Super Intelligence (SI)

The Spacy Legacy team used Artificial Intelligence (AI) as a supporting tool during the development of the project, particularly for visual content creation, writing, translation, and editing.

Most of the illustrations and 3D-style representations featured in the platform were created with the assistance of generative AI. These visuals were inspired by original spacecraft prototypes, historical photographs, technical designs, and references to real NASA exploration equipment.

The purpose of using AI-generated imagery was to make historical space artifacts more visually engaging and accessible to students and space enthusiasts.

However, not all images were AI-generated. The platform also includes authentic historical photographs and reference materials obtained from NASA sources.

AI-assisted illustrations are educational representations and may differ from the original spacecraft. They should not be interpreted as technically exact replicas or authentic mission photographs.

AI was also used to support the drafting, translation, and editing of project documentation, helping improve the clarity, organization, and accessibility of the educational content.

Scientific accuracy remains a priority. Historical mission information, including launch dates, locations, equipment functions, and scientific discoveries, is based on NASA documentation and the NASA Space Science Data Coordinated Archive (NSSDCA), rather than on AI-generated claims.

By transparently acknowledging the use of AI, Spacy Legacy demonstrates how emerging technologies can support scientific education, creativity, and accessibility while maintaining a clear distinction between verified historical information and AI-assisted content.

Sustainability and Robotics Education

Beyond telling the stories of past missions, Spacy Legacy encourages reflection on sustainability in space exploration.

The platform presents theoretical scenarios in which components from inactive space equipment could be recovered and reused. Examples include the robotic arms of the Viking 1 and InSight landers, the wheels of the Apollo 15 Lunar Roving Vehicle, and the rotors of the Ingenuity helicopter.

To transform these concepts into educational activities, we developed a three-stage teaching methodology:

  1. Identification: Recognizing components, materials, and scientific instruments found in space equipment.
  2. Robotic Reconfiguration: Exploring how robots could recover and adapt components through simulations or classroom prototypes.
  3. Cost Analysis: Calculating potential savings in transported mass and launch costs.

The educational content also introduces fundamental concepts of mobile robotics, autonomy, navigation, asynchronous communication, and control systems, including GPC and PID techniques.

The proposed component reuse scenarios are conceptual engineering ideas intended for education and research. They do not represent recovery operations that have already been carried out or technically validated.

Accessibility and Inclusion

Accessibility is one of the fundamental pillars of Spacy Legacy.

The platform provides Brazilian Sign Language resources, audio narration, multilingual support, high-contrast settings, three text-size options, reduced-motion features, and keyboard navigation.

These features aim to expand access to scientific knowledge, allowing people with different abilities and accessibility needs to explore the platform's educational content.

Impact and Creative Innovation

Spacy Legacy combines history, science, sustainability, and technological experimentation into an engaging educational experience.

Its main innovation is allowing users not only to learn about historical space equipment but also to investigate how it worked, experiment with engineering decisions, and explore potential future applications for its components.

The project aims to encourage critical thinking, robotics education, and interest in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM).

Our next steps include expanding the artifact collection, developing educational activities for teachers, introducing classroom challenges within the simulator, and providing offline access for schools with limited internet connectivity.

Our mission is to demonstrate that the end of a space mission does not mean the end of its contribution to humanity. Every artifact carries discoveries, knowledge, and possibilities capable of inspiring future generations.

Abandoned but Not Forgotten: Stories of NASA's Space Equipment Left Behind on the Moon and Mars — the legacy of space exploration lives on.
